iterations.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Required retrospective ImageGen concept review1 of max3 for OpenFA Mikotaj Ruth-Strivakh MK3C LARGE transporter. Attached contact sheet is actual paletted legacy, authoritative geometry and broad colour. Reconstruct its distinctive low crosswise open copper truss/beam structure with an elongated central slate-blue pressure body running perpendicular to that beam, and small slate-blue rounded flattened terminal pods at the two far beam ends. Preserve OPEN rectangular gaps in the copper side frames; do not fill them with armour. Several small muted green fittings sit at structural junctions. Main body is opaque rounded blue-grey metal, not a transparent glass globe; broad slightly flattened upper shell, narrower projecting underside machinery. Match the legacy relation of wide beam to relatively short central fore-aft body and thin overall height. Transport size class should inform believable material details while preserving this silhouette. Worn copper/orange structural metal, slate-blue body/pods, modest green and dull brass accents; scratches, recess grime, restrained joints and fasteners, no dense hull grid. Avoid adding cargo containers, huge antennas, new weapons, thrust plumes or invented functional mechanisms. Show one clear three-quarter studio view and smaller plan view of the SAME geometry, charcoal backdrop, no text or original pixel collage.
iterations.verdict: Broad form/material concept retained: low crosswise copper structure, opaque elongated blue central body, blue terminal pods and small green junction fittings. The plan inset resolves perpendicular body/beam axes; oblique hero alone is ambiguous. New panel/hatch patterns are not treated as legacy fact.

glb_visual_review: Actual imported GLB inspected against legacy and the concept: perpendicular central-body/beam arrangement, open copper bays, terminal pods, green fittings and low profile agree. The existing open triangulated frame is retained; filling it with the concept's thicker box sections is not required by legacy. Surface details remain restrained and authored.
